obligations.behavior: a declared body above MAX_BODY_BYTES is answered 413 + Connection: close before auth, and the next request on a fresh connection parses cleanly
obligations.source_text: oversized-body refusal (#302 item 1): _read_raw_body is byte-identical (md5 72fcf5a7) in pi, qwen, claude-code, codex, colleague, human-inbox and notify server.py and truncates at MAX_BODY_BYTES=8 MiB; notify and human-inbox already ship _refuse_oversized_body (drain in 64 KiB chunks, 413, Connection: close via _write_json(close=True)) — port that helper verbatim to the five checkout bridges and call it before _read_json_body in the invocation handler; jira's server.py already answers 413 at 1 MiB and is untouched

obligations.behavior: the drain stops after MAX_BODY_BYTES; a 10x declared length with only the cap sent still gets its 413 within the socket timeout
obligations.source_text: bounded drain (challenge / security+concurrency lens): notify's _refuse_oversized_body drains the FULL declared Content-Length before answering 413, and notify's do_POST calls it before any auth check, so an unauthenticated client declaring a huge length can hold the single-threaded server reading for as long as it keeps sending (only the 30 s per-read socket timeout bounds it); the ported helper drains at most MAX_BODY_BYTES (or a small multiple) and then closes, and the same bound goes back into notify and human-inbox so all seven stay identical
